t:
(a) Report Required.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall jointly submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report on the plans of the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs, respectively, to ensure that the most clinically appropriate prosthetics and orthotics are made available to injured members of the Armed Forces and veterans using technological advances as appropriate. Such report shall include a description of the processes of each Secretary with respect to coordinating and identifying care in the Department of Veterans Affairs for an injured member of the Armed Forces who, prior to the member being discharged or released from the Armed Forces, has an advanced technology prosthetic. 
    (b) Covered Prosthetics and Orthotics.—The prosthetics and orthotics to be covered by the report under subsection (a) shall include powered prosthetics and orthotics that will enable members of the Armed Forces and veterans who have suffered amputation and, in the case of orthotics wearers, other injuries with limb salvage, to restore functionality to the maximum extent practicable. 
    (c) Appropriate Committees of Congress Defined.—In this section, the term “appropriate committees of Congress” means—
        (1) the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate; and 
        (2) the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the joint report and the reference to "coordinating" care signal participation. But the report goes to congressional committees, and the coordination is between the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs, all of which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted or given a role in any federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall jointly submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report

opus.w: This section only requires two federal Secretaries to send a joint report to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The 'jointly' and 'coordinating' language describes cooperation between two federal agencies, not consultation with anyone outside the government. No comment period, hearing, advisory panel with outside members, outside consultation or right to sue is created.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall jointly submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report on the plans of the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading and why it fails.** The section talks about the two Secretaries "jointly" submitting a report and about "coordinating" care, which can sound like participation. But every actor named is inside the federal government: the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and congressional committees. A report to Congress and coordination between agencies are both listed traps. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted before any federal decision.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section requires a report to be submitted to Congress by two federal Secretaries. Congress and federal agencies are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress and coordination between federal agencies from the definition of participation. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside party (such as states, tribes, or the public).
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall jointly submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report involves coordination between the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs, it constitutes "participation" or "consultation." However, both entities are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. Furthermore, the report is submitted *to* Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts, etc.) in the decision-making process described here.
